author: Chicago City Wire
title: Rush Medical College Alumni Association president reflects on achievements and urges continued support
text:
This past year marked a significant period for Rush Medical College and its alumni community. David Margolin, President of the Rush Medical College Alumni Association, reflected on recent milestones in a message to fellow graduates.
Margolin recounted his experience at the White Coat Ceremony, where he addressed incoming students and praised the Admissions Committee for selecting 144 new members for the RMC Class of 2029 out of over 13,000 applicants. He highlighted the impact of Vice Dean Lee Jones’s remarks on patient care and Dr. Robert Higgins’s comments regarding student support during challenging times.
Margolin noted that “Rush continues to attract exceptional leaders, including Dr. Pete Batra, the recently appointed dean of Rush Medical College. I look forward to working with him as Rush continues to grow. Even amidst this growth, Rush remains grounded in the values that drew many of us here: innovative teaching, strong clinical preparation, community engagement and an unwavering commitment to health equity. I see these values firsthand every year when I interview applicants whose accomplishments and service inspire me and make me proud to be a Rush graduate.”
He also emphasized ongoing efforts by the alumni association to enhance support for future physicians at Rush: “The RMCAA is committed to supporting these future physicians and matching the excellence we see throughout the institution. We are exploring new ways to deepen our impact and strengthen support for students. Personally, in 2025 I started a scholarship for RMC students in the name of my son, Aaron Lloyd Margolin. Our goal is to ensure that our work continues to uplift students so they can embody the excellence of Rush.”
Margolin encouraged alumni contributions toward student success funds: “Please consider making a gift to the RMC Student Success Fund. Your support helps ease the financial burden for students, many of whom graduate with significant debt.”
Rush University Medical Center is based in Chicago, Illinois and has operated since 1837 as both a hospital and training institution under current president Dr. Omar Lateef.
Margolin concluded by stating: “Rush is an outstanding institution, and it is through the support of alumni like you and me that we help carry it forward on its path of continued success, growth, service and impact.”
